cross_paper_synthesis.consensus: There is no consensus or explicit scientific explanation provided in the available text regarding why specific sub-zero temperatures (−20 °C or −25 °C) were selected for electro-polishing AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA, nor is there any analysis of the consequences of varying these conditions.
cross_paper_synthesis.different_approaches: The two available answers address the same material (AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA) but focus on distinct preparation stages and specific unanswered questions. One approach focuses on the TEM specimen preparation at −20 °C, noting the lack of rationale for temperature selection and amorphization prevention. The other approach focuses on EBSD specimen preparation at −25 °C, noting the absence of analysis regarding selective etching and phase contrast bias.
cross_paper_synthesis.condition_dependencies: The documented conditions are temperature-dependent: 10 vol% nitric acid alcohol solution is used at −25 °C for EBSD [8760d564e3da9f1d] and −20 °C for TEM [ad3406022e3928fd]. The specific temperature thresholds appear critical to the protocol but their functional dependence on microstructural preservation is not defined in the text.
cross_paper_synthesis.contradictions: There are no genuine contradictions between the answers; however, they represent a gap in knowledge where the text cites the conditions but fails to provide the mechanistic justification requested by the question variants.
cross_paper_synthesis.evidence_strength: The evidence is strictly observational and negative. The answers confirm the existence of specific protocols but explicitly state 'no analysis', 'no explanation', 'no rationale provided', and 'mechanism: Not specified' [8760d564e3da9f1d, ad3406022e3928fd].
cross_paper_synthesis.unresolved_gap: The primary unresolved gap is the lack of mechanistic understanding in the source text regarding why −20 °C and −25 °C are necessary to prevent amorphization during twin-jet polishing or to ensure phase contrast fidelity in EBSD maps without selective etching bias.
cross_paper_synthesis.candidate_hypothesis: Sub-zero temperatures are likely required to suppress thermal activation of amorphous phase formation during ion milling or electro-polishing and to control dissolution kinetics to prevent selective etching of specific phases in the HEA.
cross_paper_synthesis.discriminating_experiment: Compare microstructural outcomes (amorphous layer thickness, phase contrast fidelity) of samples polished at room temperature versus −20 °C and −25 °C using the same 10 vol% nitric acid alcohol solution to quantify the suppression of amorphization and etching bias.
